name: The Spire Ascendancy Ball — Corponation Cultural Summit
creator: Axiom-HelixCorp Joint Cultural Council; administered by the Spire Residency Board
description: Held on the first Saturday of November in the Spire's uppermost public tier — the Aurelius Crown, a climate-controlled garden complex above the cloud line — the Ascendancy Ball is the single most exclusive annual event in Meridian 88, combining a formal gala with a curated showcase of corponation-sponsored art, performance, and technology. Attendance is by invitation only, with the guest list functioning as an informal index of Spire power; being removed from the list is considered a significant social and professional sanction. The event is broadcast via luxury neural feed to Tier 4 subscribers as a prestige package, offering curated sensory highlights but carefully excluding the actual guest interactions and conversations.
medium: physical / luxury neural broadcast (Tier 4 subscription) / curated holographic highlights (Tier 3)
cultural_impact: The Ascendancy Ball functions as an annual recalibration of Spire social hierarchy — alliances are signaled, exclusions are noted, and the art and technology showcased serves as a preview of what the corponations intend to normalize in the coming year.
controversy: A 2220 data leak published the full internal guest seating arrangements for the previous five Balls, revealing a systematic pattern of using table proximity as a tool to manage mergers, acquisitions, and political favors — the leak was attributed to a disgruntled Spire domestic worker and was suppressed within 18 hours.
story_hooks: A Tier 2 caterer working the Ascendancy Ball overhears a conversation that suggests a major corponation merger will eliminate the Shelf district where their family lives — and they have one evening to decide what to do with that information.

A Tier 4 subscriber watching the luxury neural broadcast notices something in the curated feed that shouldn't be there — a face, a conversation fragment, something the editing team missed — that implicates a Spire figure in something serious.

An artist whose work is being showcased at the Ball discovers, hours before the event, that the piece has been subtly altered by the curatorial team to remove its original political meaning — and the original version still exists on a pirate neural feed.
